---
title: Build a connector host
description: Write the program that redeems a one-time link, learns which plugin connectors to run on its machine, gets each one's key, and runs it with its settings and mapping.
job: A builder writes a connector host, the program that runs a plugin's connectors with keys it gets from Marfa.
kind: how-to
---

A **connector host** is the program that runs [a plugin's connectors](/use/run-a-plugin-connector) on a machine the owner linked. Marfa doesn't publish one yet. The [connector kit](/reference/connector-kit) takes the key its host mints and refuses others, so the operations below mint it.

## Redeem the link

The owner gives the host a one-time link, such as `https://marfa.example.com/connect#marfa_l1_…`. The instance's address comes before `/connect`, and the code after the `#`. [Send the code](/reference/api/connector-hosts/redeemConnectorHostLink) with no credential:

```http
POST /connector-hosts/redeem
Content-Type: application/json

{ "code": "marfa_l1_4f4f4f4f…" }
```

The answer holds the host's `id`, `name` and own `key`. **Keep the key where only the host reads it.** It holds `connectors.host` alone, which opens only the two operations below; every other answers `401`. A link that ended, or was used, answers `404 connector_link_not_found`, and the owner makes another with `marfa hosts link`.

## Learn what to run

```http
GET /connector-hosts/self
Authorization: Bearer $HOST_KEY
```

`connectors` lists each plugin connector assigned to the host, with its `plugin`, `version`, the plugin's `connector` section, `key_minted`, and what the owner [asked of it](/use/pause-or-run-a-connector): `paused`, and `run_requested_at` when the owner asked for a run now. **The host does not start a paused connector.** A run already under way finishes, and Marfa still takes its writes ([`plugins/pause-writes-land`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/plugins.md#pluginspause-writes-land)). Start one the owner asked to run now. Ask on start and often: a connector that leaves the list has moved, and lost its key.

Where the section names `code`, fetch the connector from its `url`, and **run the file only when its SHA-256 matches `sha256`.**

## Get each connector's key

```http
POST /connector-hosts/self/connectors/rss/key
Authorization: Bearer $HOST_KEY
```

The answer's `key` holds the connector's `source`, and write on its kinds' types and its `edge_types`. **Each mint revokes the key minted before,** so keep the key and mint again only when it's lost or refused. `404 plugin_not_found` means the connector no longer runs here.

## Run the connector with it

Start it with the key and `MARFA_API_URL`, wake it for a run now, and stop it once it leaves the list. The rest is the connector's, which the [kit](/reference/connector-kit) does for you. It [registers](/reference/api/connectors/registerConnector), then on each run:

1. **Reads what the owner asked** with [`GET /plugins/{name}/connector`](/reference/api/plugins/getPluginConnector), and skips the run if `paused` is `true`.
2. **Reads its settings** with [`GET /connectors/{id}/settings`](/reference/api/connector-state/getConnectorSettings), with its secrets opened to this key alone. A secret with `unreadable` `true` needs the owner to set it again.
3. **Reads its mapping** with [`GET /plugins/{name}/connector/mapping`](/reference/api/plugins/getConnectorMapping), and writes each enabled kind as the type and tier it names, filling each field from its `from`, `fixed` or `template`.
4. **Carries out each request under `rewrites`:** it moves its own items on each type `from` lists for a kind onto that kind's target with `retype: true`, then [sends back the request's `number`](/reference/api/plugins/finishConnectorRewrite). Until then, on a type the kind was mapped onto before, it may read and move its own items and write nothing else.
5. **Answers each pending preview** from [`GET /plugins/{name}/connector/previews`](/reference/api/plugins/listMappingPreviews): it renders the preview's `kind` under its `mapping` on the item `item_id` names, or a recent one, and [sends](/reference/api/plugins/answerMappingPreview) what it filled as `result`, at most 64 KiB, or why it couldn't as `error`, within 10 minutes.
6. **Reports the run** with [`POST /connectors/{id}/runs`](/reference/api/connectors/reportConnectorRun), naming the `run_requested_at` it read, so the owner's request clears.

**On a target type its key doesn't reach, the connector reads and writes only its own items,** and the links from them of edge types its key reads. It [lists](/reference/api/items/listItems) them with any filter, reads each one's edges, versions, extensions and table rows, follows their events, keeps their agreements and settles their tombstones. Search, views, exports, a working copy and MCP's read tools answer by its key alone.

Its state document, problems and agreements stay with its source on the instance, so a connector moved to another host resumes where it stopped ([Keep your place](/build/connector-without-the-kit#keep-your-place)).

The rules behind this page are in the [plugins](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/plugins.md#a-hosts-key) and [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md#a-plugin-connectors-settings) chapters of the contract.
